C04_S02 FRESH SCHUR-CENTRAL DEPTH DERIVATION

STATUS AND ORIGIN

Root proposed the column-wedge construction and, subsequently, the exact
row-count lower bound. This artifact reconstructs both arguments independently
of c04_s03 and without reading another worker's new Schur proof. Earlier own
files, including INITIAL and the spin proof package, are preserved.

The main claims below are proved as elementary consequences of the standard
Schur-Weyl decomposition and highest-weight structure of its U(d) modules.
They have an explicit continuous product-cluster ensemble. This is internal
mathematical verification, not an external validation or novelty certificate.
A directly relevant 2026 isotypic-entanglement paper is being read separately;
the upper construction should be described as an elementary Schur-Weyl
corollary unless priority is established by more than a search.

1. DEFINITIONS AND EXACT QUANTIFIERS

Let N>=1, d>=1 and H=(C^d)^tensor N, with the defining local representation.
Write U_N=U^tensor N and W_pi for site permutations pi in S_N.
A pure state is k-producible if it is a tensor product over a partition of
the N sites into clusters of size at most k. A mixed state is k-producible if
it is a convex mixture of such pure states; partitions may differ between
mixture terms. Its entanglement depth is the least such k, in [1,N].

Theorem A. If a density matrix rho satisfies
  U_N rho U_N*=rho for every U in U(d),
  W_pi rho W_pi*=rho for every pi in S_N,
then rho is min(d,N)-producible. More precisely, for every partition lambda
of N with r=ell(lambda)<=d, its normalized isotypic projector
  omega_lambda=P_lambda/Tr(P_lambda)
has entanglement depth EXACTLY r. Every density matrix whose support is
contained in that single isotypic subspace has depth at least r.

Theorem B. Any product of invertible local filters preserves entanglement
depth exactly. In particular, for one invertible g on C^d,
  omega_lambda,g = g_N P_lambda g_N*/Tr(g_N P_lambda g_N*)
has exact depth r, and g_N rho g_N*/Tr(g_N rho g_N*) is min(d,N)-producible
for rho in Theorem A. Here g_N=g^tensor N.

Theorem C. Let Z be any Hermitian operator scalar on each Schur-Weyl
isotypic subspace: Z=sum_lambda z_lambda P_lambda, z_lambda real. Let B be
any Hermitian d by d matrix and J_B=sum_i B_i. Then
  rho=exp(Z+J_B)/Tr exp(Z+J_B)
is min(d,N)-producible, at every finite N and all finite real p

c04_s03 — CENTRAL SCHUR STATES AND EXACT SINGLE-SECTOR DEPTH
7 October 2026 UTC. New artifact; earlier INITIAL and FINAL are preserved.
Root supplied both candidate mechanisms. All steps below are reconstructed
independently. The column construction has a direct prior antecedent:
Reuvers, arXiv:1805.00364v2, Lemma 13, Eq. (61). It is NOT claimed as new.
The depth lower bound is internally proved here; external validation and
priority remain UNKNOWN. Root assigned c04_s02 a separate independent audit.

C1. NOTATION AND PRECISE RESULTS
Let H=(C^d)^{tensor N}, with N>=1, d>=2. For a partition lambda of N
with at most d rows, let
 H = direct_sum_lambda U_lambda tensor M_lambda
be Schur-Weyl decomposition. U_lambda is the irreducible polynomial U(d)
representation of highest weight lambda, padded with zeros to d entries;
M_lambda is the irreducible S_N representation. Write P_lambda for the
orthogonal projector onto the ENTIRE isotypic space U_lambda tensor M_lambda,
u_lambda=dim U_lambda, m_lambda=dim M_lambda, and ell(lambda) for its number
of nonzero rows. Thus Tr P_lambda = u_lambda m_lambda.

A pure k-producible vector factors over a partition of the labeled particles
into clusters, each of size at most k. A k-producible density is a convex
mixture of such pure vectors, allowing different partitions in different terms.
Entanglement depth is the least such k.

Theorem:
 (i) P_lambda/(u_lambda m_lambda) has depth EXACTLY ell(lambda).
 (ii) EVERY density supported entirely in this isotypic space has depth
      at least ell(lambda). It need not obey the matching upper bound.
 (iii) Every density invariant under BOTH U^{tensor N} for all U in U(d)
       and conjugation by every site permutation is d-producible.
       More precisely its depth is at most max_{q_lambda>0} ell(lambda).
 (iv) Any common local filter A^{tensor N}, conditioned on a nonzero outcome,
      preserves the upper bound in (iii). A filtered single normalized
      P_lambda still has depth exactly ell(lambda), even for singular A
      whenever its outcome is nonzero.
These results do not apply the upper bound to arbitrary Werner states
without permutation invariance. They do not give a matching lower bound
for arbitrary mixtures of lambda sectors.

C04_S02 SCHUR FILTER ENVELOPE AND PRIORITY ADDENDUM

READ THIS WITH SCHUR_CENTRAL_EXACT_DEPTH.txt. The earlier artifact is preserved.
This addendum supersedes its Section 9 coarse filtering-cost caution with a
proved block-dependent envelope. It also records the acquired exact antecedent
of the column-wedge construction, supplied as a priority lead by root/c09_s01.

1. SHARP SPECTRAL ENVELOPE: EXPECTED POLYNOMIAL REJECTION

Let g be any supplied invertible local filter and E=g*g. Its eigenvalues are
a_1>=...>=a_d>0. Define
  M_lambda=product_{i=1}^d a_i^{lambda_i},
  t_lambda(U)=product_columns det[(U*EU)_{1:h_c,1:h_c}].
For each height h, the determinant is the expectation of the positive operator
wedge^h E on the unit vector Ue_1 wedge ... wedge Ue_h. Its operator norm is
product_{i<=h} a_i. Multiplying over columns gives the exact envelope
  0<t_lambda(U)<=M_lambda.

The Haar mean from the main proof is
  A_lambda=chi_lambda(E)/D_lambda.
The polynomial GL(d) representation of E is positive Hermitian. Its largest
eigenvalue is M_lambda: write log E in a dominant diagonal Cartan chamber;
the highest weight lambda maximizes the weight pairing. This eigenvalue occurs
in the character trace, with positive multiplicity, so
  M_lambda<=chi_lambda(E)<=D_lambda M_lambda.
Consequently rejection from Haar U with acceptance t_lambda(U)/M_lambda has
  alpha_lambda=A_lambda/M_lambda in [1/D_lambda,1],
and expected trials at most D_lambda, INDEPENDENT of cond(g) and field size.

For fixed d,
  D_lambda=product_{i<j}(lambda_i-lambda_j+j-i)/(j-i)
            <=(N+d)^{d(d-1)/2}/product_{i<j}(j-i).
Each proposal needs only d by d operations, at most d different Gram
determinants, and integer powers from the column multiplicities
m_h=lambda_h-lambda_{h+1}. Emit the normalized product of the filtered
column wedges and independently assign a uniform site permutation.
No Schur-transform circuit and no exponentially large full state vector are
needed for this ensemble construction.

This proves an expected polynomial proposal count for fixed d in an exact
real-arithmetic interface. It is a strict improvement over the valid but
unnecessarily coarse ||g||^(2N) rejection envelope in the preserved proof.
The old exponential upper bound must not be read as an impossibility result.
